articles.title: Hubble Revisits a Globular Cluster's Age
articles.summary: The article presents three distinct astronomical reports: Hubble's re-examination of the globular cluster IC 4499 refined its age to approximately 12 billion years, aligning it with other Milky Way clusters, and supported the theory that less massive clusters typically host a single stellar generation. Separately, the VLT Survey Telescope captured a highly detailed image of the Triangulum Galaxy (Messier 33), showcasing its star clusters and glowing gas clouds. Lastly, an update on solar activity for early August noted a high sunspot count and a significant prominence, alongside a reminder for safe solar observation.

articles.title: SJAA Yosemite Trip July 2014
articles.summary: The article recounts the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) successful astronomy trip to Yosemite in July 2014, where volunteers showcased celestial objects like Saturn, Iridium Flares, M55, and the Pleiades to a diverse international audience. Despite initial concerns about fire and clouds, the event was a highlight, marked by memorable observations and public engagement, thanks to the efforts of numerous SJAA volunteers.

articles.title: Grandview Campground Trip Report – July 2014
articles.summary: This article is a trip report from Gary Chock and Jose Marte detailing their astronomy observation visit to Grandview Campground in Inyo National Forest during July 2014. They experienced exceptional dark sky conditions, excellent seeing, and transparency, allowing for detailed views of numerous celestial objects including the Milky Way, M7, M13, and M51. The report also includes practical information about the campground, weather conditions, and tips for planning future trips to this high-altitude observing site.

articles.title: Celebrate Cambrian Festival
articles.summary: The Celebrate Cambrian Festival, held on August 24, 2014, brought together residents of San Jose's Cambrian area for a day of community activities. The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) participated for the fifth consecutive year, with President Rob Jaworski and volunteers offering solar observing equipment to entertain attendees.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This 'Kid Spot' section offers astronomy-themed entertainment and educational content for children. It features space-related jokes, a short quiz about planets and telescopes, and a 'Night Sky Challenge' for September 2014, encouraging kids to spot celestial objects like Mercury, Spica, Antares, and Saturn.

articles.title: Constellations
articles.summary: The article provides an overview of the constellation Cygnus, detailing its history, optimal visibility in the Northern Hemisphere, and characteristic features including the Northern Cross asterism. It highlights key stars like Deneb (part of the Summer Triangle) and the binary Albireo, a favorite among amateur astronomers. Additionally, it describes several deep-sky objects located within Cygnus due to its position on the Milky Way, such as open clusters M39 and NGC 6910, and the prominent North America Nebula (NGC 7000).

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides diverse programs for its members and the public, including educational school star parties and monthly public solar observing sessions at Houge Park. Members can access an astronomy library, participate in an advanced loaner telescope program for equipment evaluation, and utilize a monthly Fix-It program for gear repair. Additionally, the club supports binocular stargazing events to introduce basic astronomy to the public.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced Bill O'Neil as a new Board member and shared plans for commemorating the club's upcoming 60th anniversary. Excerpts from the August 2014 Board meeting revealed a decision to change the Ephemeris newsletter's publication frequency from monthly to quarterly starting next calendar year, along with approval for new tools for the FixIt Program. Other updates included potential changes to the solar observing program and the introduction of a volunteer for the equipment donation program.
